recommendedTextbook.title: WABP Junior Secondary Business Studies Book 2
recommendedTextbook.author: Ehiametalor, E. T., Makore, C., & Awoyemi, M. O.
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

topics.topic: Consumer Rights and Consumer Protection Agencies
subtopics: Rights of consumers: Right to safety, information, choice, hearing, redress
Statutory consumer protection agencies: FCCPC, SON, NAFDAC, CPC
Procedure for seeking redress when supplied defective goods or fake products
objectives: List 6 fundamental universal rights of consumers
State specific regulatory mandates of NAFDAC and Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON)
Draft a formal complaint letter seeking refund for sub-standard merchandise

topics.topic: Trade: Wholesale and Retail Trade Dynamics
subtopics: Wholesale trade: Functions to manufacturer and to retailer
Retail trade: Itinerant trading, roadside shops, supermarkets, convenience stores
Distribution channels and reasons for eliminating the middleman
objectives: Distinguish wholesalers from retailers in Nigerian trade channels
Explain how wholesalers finance small-scale producers through cash advances
Evaluate consumer price effects of buying directly from factories

topics.topic: Bookkeeping: Source Documents and Business Transactions
subtopics: Meaning and purpose of commercial source documents
Types: Invoice, proforma invoice, receipt, credit note, debit note, payment voucher
Extracting accounting figures from transaction slips in Naira
objectives: Explain the difference between a Debit Note and a Credit Note
Fill out a standard commercial receipt and payment voucher accurately

topics.topic: The Cash Book: Single-Column Cash Book
subtopics: Meaning, ruling, and format of a single-column Cash Book
Debit entries (receipts of cash) vs credit entries (payments of cash)
Balancing the Cash Book: Balance c/d and b/d
objectives: Rule a standard single-column Cash Book with date, particulars, folio, amount
Post 10 hypothetical cash transactions into the Cash Book
Calculate closing balance and bring down opening balance for the new trading month
